Summary: The paper introduces adaptive Time Delay Stability (aTDS), data-driven rules for the TDS window, lag range and tolerance, and evaluates them on synthetic signals with known coupling against published, hand-rescaled and oracle settings, across signal classes, on one EEG pair and in synthetic networks with per-link rotation tests and BH-FDR. The revision adds a justification of the default window rule, a discussion of null-model biases and of the oracle, practical guidance and a summary of the evidence.
Strengths: Addresses a genuine reproducibility and transferability problem of TDS with principled, fully specified rules.
Careful evaluation with isolated ablations, generous baselines, paired intervals and equivalence testing.
Important negative result on fixed lag ranges.
Revised version is transparent about null-model biases and gives concrete usage guidance.
Honest scope; code and data released.
Weaknesses: No staged or multi-subject real data; practical benefit for sleep networks not demonstrated.
Design constants other than 30 not varied.
Null-model and SE biases described only qualitatively.
Joint B_xy supported by one configuration.
Even capped windows span several sleep epochs; not stated explicitly.
Questions: How would per-stage calibration on a staged cohort change network contrasts?
What is the per-link power in the slow-down experiment?
Can the out-of-range diagnostic be automated?
Limitations: Synthetic evidence dominates; one real pair.
Time resolution coarser than sleep epochs.
